name: Name
body:
Over a four-week period, players will grow a WARMACHINE force as they gain familiarity with the rules and experience with the models in their chosen army.
Each week is structured around a new scenario designed to teach players specific aspects of the game. As players complete the weekly scenarios, they will earn commendations for their achievement and at the end of all four weeks will receive a reward.
The Journeyman League is appropriate for new and experienced players alike. Experienced players can be a great boon to a Journeyman League and are encouraged to help new players learn the rules along the way.

name: Name
body:
Participants in the league are encouraged to play two matches per week, ideally against different opponents. With each match played, players earn a Commendation recognizing their advancement in expanding their force and learning the new aspects of the game. If for any reason someone misses a week or a Commendation, it’s always acceptable for them to make up the game and get their Commendation at a later time. The important aspect is to get the experience each week offers.
The Journeyman League kit consists of four Universal Widgets. The Widgets are highly useful tools that enable players to quickly measure many common distances referenced in the game. The Universal Widgets should be made available to players on league nights during the four-week league and awarded to players who achieve at least six out of the eight possible Commendations during the course of the league.

name: Name
body:
Leagues benefit from consistency, so determining a weekly league night from the outset is highly recommended. Naturally, we recommend Wednesday, because "WARMACHINE Wednesday" has a great ring to it that players won’t forget. But the most important thing is to make sure the league is held at a consistent time that all participants can commit to reliably showing up for.
A successful league needs an organizer. The organizer can be a store staff member, a community leader, or even a participant in the league. It just needs to be someone that can help establish the league meeting time and manage the rewards.

name: Name
body:
Players will learn the basics of play using a Leader and a pair of Cohort models with preconfigured spell racks and load outs. By the end of the match, players should understand the phases of a turn, how to allocate focus, moving through rough terrain and over obstacles, using cover, charging, and power attacks.
Force Composition: 30 Points
-1 Leader
-2 Warjacks (Load Outs Preconfigured)
-Spell Racks: Preconfigured
-No Command Cards Used
Map Size: 36" x 36"

name: Name
body: Players earn points by navigating the terrain elements on the battlefield while performing basic combat actions.

name: Name
body:
Players roll a d6 to determine who goes first, then they take turns placing four pieces of terrain each. Each player must place at least one piece of rough terrain and one piece of terrain that can provide cover.
The first player deploys 7" from their chosen table edge. The second player deploys 10" from their table edge.

name: Name
body:
Players earn points for destroying their opponent’s models:
-Heavy Cohort Model—3 points
-Light Cohort Model—2 Points
-No points are scored for destroying the opponent’s Leader
A player can score 1 point for completing any of the following items, but each item can only be scored once per match:
-Moving a model through rough terrain
-Moving a model over an obstacle
-Placing a model in cover
-Charging an enemy model
-Boosting an attack or damage roll
-Casting a spell
-Executing a power attack

name: Name
body:
The first player who has 9 points at the end of any round wins.
At the end of five rounds, if no player has scored 9 points, the player with the most points wins.

name: Name
body:
Players expand their force with a solo and unit and learn the strategic benefits of Command Cards, unlock the secret of spell channeling, and experience the power of feats, all while continuing to gain experience in the basics of combat.
Force Composition: 30 Points
-1 Leader
-1–2 Warjacks: Customizable
-1 Unit
-1 Solo
-Spell Rack: Preconfigured
-Command Cards: Preconfigured

name: Name
body: Map Size: 36" x 36"

name: Name
body: Players earn points by executing power attacks, moving through rough terrain or over obstacles, finding cover, and eliminating their opponent’s warjacks.

name: Name
body:
Players roll a d6 to determine who goes first, then they take turns placing four pieces of terrain each. Each player must place at least one piece of elevated terrain.
The first player deploys 7" from their chosen table edge. The second player deploys 10" from their table edge.

name: Name
body:
Players earn points for destroying their opponent’s models:
-Heavy Cohort Model—3 points
-Light Cohort Model—2 Points
-Entire Unit—2 points
- Solo—1 point
-No points are scored for destroying the opponent’s Leader

name: Name
body:
A player can score 1 point for completing any of the following items, but each item can only be scored once per match:
-Aiming a ranged attack
-Gaining a defense bonus from elevation
-Disengaging from melee
-Charging an enemy model with a unit
-Channeling  a spell through an arc node or executing a power attack
-Using a Command Card
-Running a warjack
-Use a Leader’s feat

name: Name
body:
The first player who has 9 points at the end of any round wins.
At the end of five rounds, if no player has scored 9 points, the player with the most points wins.

name: Name
body:
Players expand their force with an additional unit and command attachments and customize their spell rack and warjack loadouts before fighting strategic locations on the battlefield.
Force Composition: 50 Points
-1 Leader
-1–2 Warjacks
-1–2 Units
-1–2 Command Attachments
-1 Solo
-Spell Rack: Customizable
-Command Cards: Preconfigured

name: Name
body: Map Size: 48" x 48"

name: Name
body: Players earn points by securing terrain objectives on the battlefield.

name: Name
body: Place three terrain objectives on the battlefield as shown on the map below. A terrain objective should be about 3"–5" across so it is large enough to position multiple models around it or on top of it. Hills, buildings, and ruins make excellent terrain objectives, but anything can be used so long as models can be placed next to or on top it.

name: Name
body:
Players roll a d6 to determine who goes first, then they take turns placing four pieces of terrain each.
The first player deploys 7" from their chosen table edge. The second player deploys 10" from their table edge.

name: Name
body:
A terrain objective is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the terrain objective uncontested.
A terrain objective is contested if both players have at least one model within 1" of the terrain objective when scoring would occur. A terrain objective is uncontested if only one player has models within 1" of the terrain objective when scoring would occur.

name: Name
body:
Players gain 1 point at the end of each turn for each terrain objective they have secured.
Players gain 3 points at the end of a turn if they secure a terrain objective that was secured by their opponent at the beginning of the active player’s turn.
A player can score 1 point for completing any of the following items, but each item can only be scored once per match:
-Damaging the opponent’s Leader
-Reducing damage to a Leader by spending focus
-Healing a Leader by spending focus

name: Name
body:
The first player who has 7 points at the end of any round wins.
At the end of five rounds, if no player has scored 7 points, the player with the most points wins.

name: Name
body:
Players compose a full 50-point force with no restrictions and then battle for glory as they experience, for the first time, the vulnerability of their Leader.
Force Composition: 50 Points
-Leader
-No model restrictions
-Warjacks: Customizable
-Spell Racks: Customizable
-Command Cards: Customizable
Map Size: 48" x 48"

name: Name
body: Players earn points by capturing small objectives and securing terrain objectives on the battlefield with additional points gained the longer they can keep those objectives secured.

name: Name
body:
Place two terrain objectives on the battlefield as shown on the map below. A terrain objective should be about 3"–5" across so it is large enough to position multiple models around it or on top of it. Hills, buildings, and ruins make excellent terrain objectives, but anything can be used so long as models can be placed next to or on top it.
Place three small objectives on the battlefield as shown on the map below. Small objectives should be about 1"–2" across. Barrels, crates, and treasures chests make excellent small objectives, but you can use anything of the appropriate size to represent small objectives.

name: Name
body:
Players roll a d6 to determine who goes first, then they take turns placing four pieces of terrain each.
The first player deploys 7" from their chosen table edge. The second player deploys 10" from their table edge.

name: Name
body:
A terrain objective or small objective is secured when a player has two or models within 1" of the objective uncontested.
A terrain objective or small objective is contested if both players have models within 1" of the objective when scoring would occur. A terrain objective or small objective is uncontested if only one player has models within 1" of the objective when scoring would occur.

name: Name
body:
Players gain 1 point at the end of each turn for each terrain objective they have secured.
Players gain 3 points at the end of a turn if they secure a terrain objective that was secured by their opponent at the beginning of the active player’s turn.
At the beginning of any player’s turn, if they are securing a small objective, they gain 2 points and the small objective is removed from the map.
A player gains 3 points if they destroy their opponent’s Leader.

name: Name
body:
The first player who has 7 points at the end of any round wins.
At the end of five rounds or at the end of any turn in which one player no longer has a Leader, if no player has scored 7 points, the player with the most points wins.

name: Name
body: Once players have played through the scenarios, they should have a firm grasp of the rules of the game and are ready to begin experimenting. Maintaining a weekly meeting time to play will allow players to continue to gain experience with their armies while they grow and customize them over time. Scenarios and an ongoing campaign can be found in the WARMACHINE app library for app subscribers, and those scenarios provide a great source of continued entertainment for small and large groups alike.
